Whale sighted; Ahab's farewell to mast-head, recalls Parsee prophecy
Sharks follow Ahab's boat; Starbuck's foreboding, hawk and flag

evidence.quote: The old man’s hinted thought was true. Upon mustering the company, the Parsee was not there.
What’s that he said? he should still go before me, my pilot; and yet to be seen again?
the half torn body of the Parsee was seen
the tidings that the Parsee was nowhere to be found.
this then is the hearse that thou didst promise
There’s a riddle now
The ship! The hearse!—the second hearse!
Where is the second hearse?
drive off that hawk! see! he pecks—he tears the vane
A sky-hawk that tauntingly had followed the main-truck downwards
he was shot out of the boat
the treacherous line felt that double strain and tug, it snapped
whether these sharks swim to feast on the whale or on Ahab?
he was shot out of the boat
the coffin life-buoy shot lengthwise from the sea
Sink all coffins and all hearses to one common pool!
The unharming sharks, they glided by as if with padlocks on their mouths
maliciously snapped at the blades of the oars
I am old;—shake hands with me, man.
Starbuck, of late I’ve felt strangely moved to thee
Heart of wrought steel!” murmured Starbuck
Oh, my captain, my captain!—noble heart—go not—go not!
Ahab is for ever Ahab, man.
old Ahab is untouched
not too late is it, even now, the third day, to desist.
Away, mates, to the ship!
we near him.
he darted his fierce iron, and his far fiercer curse into the hated whale.
he bore down upon its advancing prow
smote the ship’s starboard bow
Diving beneath the settling ship
Thus, I give up the spear!
the great shroud of the sea rolled on
The drama’s done.
Muster the men.
Upon mustering the company
the attentive ship having descried the whole fight
again came bearing down to the rescue
His ivory leg had been snapped off
even with a broken bone, old Ahab is untouched
sat due eastward for the earliest sun.
The morning of the third day dawned fair and fresh
Stand by to sway me up!
Ahab descried the spout again
He gave the word; and still gazing round him
In due time the boats were lowered
